**Invalidate cached closures when a merge clears reach witnesses.**

`Journal::push` clears all retained reach memberships after every successful `Mutation::Merge`, but `Graph::merge_nodes` does not clear `State::closures`. A later selected read can use the stale cached closure and call `Journal::reach_path` for a member whose witness was cleared. `Witnesses::path` then panics instead of returning a verification error. This can crash public causal verification for an accepted untrusted proof sequence.

<details><summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
         self.observe_change(Mutation::Merge { keep, discard }, None);
+        st.closures.borrow_mut().clear(st.edges.len());

```

**Reject v6/v7 tags when the decoded proof does not need that layout.**

`encode` picks its tag from the proof's content:
- v7 only when some branch has `introduction_only`.
- v6 only when some merge has `current`.

`decode` accepts a v7 tag when no branch is `introduction_only`. It also accepts a v6 tag when no merge has `current` support. The only requirement is that some other native evidence exists, for example a clash with `current`. The decoded `DlProof` then re-encodes under v6 or v5.

As a result, two different byte strings decode to the same proof value. `DlProof::digest()` and `ServiceProof::digest()` of the decoded value then differ from the digest of the received bytes. The existing v5 guard on this line shows that the decoder is meant to reject layouts the proof does not need. Apply the same rule to v6 and v7.
